Switch to a generation model to create the embeddings instead
Batch embedding requests and run ingestion in parallel within limits
Skip embeddings and store raw text as the only index field

stem: Token usage for one application doubled overnight with no traffic increase. What should the team investigate first?

choices.text: The AWS Region's electricity pricing for the previous calendar month and quarter
Whether the application's logo was updated in the mobile app
The number of engineers with console access to the account
Recent prompt or retrieval changes that increased input tokens per request

stem: A team wants to evaluate a RAG application end to end, including retrieval quality and answer correctness, using a managed service. Which option fits?

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor performance checks
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases evaluation (RAG evaluation)
AWS X-Ray service maps for the application
Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canary scripts on a schedule

stem: A team wants every prompt or model change automatically scored against a fixed set of reference questions before deployment. Which TWO elements are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A policy of testing only when users report problems
A single metric based on average response length
Manual spot checks after every production deployment
An evaluation stage in CI/CD with pass thresholds
A curated golden dataset with expected answers or criteria

stem: A team needs to evaluate open-ended answers for helpfulness at scale when no single reference answer exists. Which method fits?

choices.text: LLM-as-a-judge with a rubric, validated by periodic human review
Measuring answer length and preferring the longest ones
Counting how many product names appear in each answer
Exact string matching against one reference answer per question

stem: An agent repeatedly calls the same tool in a loop without finishing. Which TWO fixes help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Remove the tool so the agent answers from general knowledge
Increase the temperature so the agent tries other actions
Improve the tool description and return clearer, structured results
Double the session timeout to give the loop more time
Set a maximum number of iterations or tool calls per request

stem: A Bedrock Agent chooses the wrong action group for some requests. Which tool helps diagnose why?

choices.text: The S3 access logs for the knowledge base's data bucket
The agent trace showing its reasoning and orchestration steps
The IAM credential report for the entire AWS account
The VPC Flow Logs for the application's private subnets

stem: After a model upgrade, JSON outputs occasionally fail schema validation. Which approach is most robust?

choices.text: Validate outputs, retry with the error message, and use tool schemas for structure
Remove validation so downstream systems accept whatever the model returns
Roll back permanently and never upgrade the model again for this application or its successors
Increase temperature so that the model tries different JSON structures

stem: A RAG assistant answers correctly in testing but returns 'no information found' for many production questions. Investigation shows production documents were never synced. What fixes this?

choices.text: Increase the generation model's context window to its maximum available setting for all queries
Run and automate the knowledge base ingestion job for the production data source
Switch the vector store engine without changing the ingestion process
Rewrite the system prompt to tell the model to try harder to answer

stem: Before launch, a team wants to test how the assistant handles adversarial inputs such as jailbreaks and data exfiltration attempts. Which practice fits?

choices.text: Load testing with thousands of identical benign requests
A survey asking users if they feel the assistant is safe
Red-team testing with a curated set of adversarial prompts
Unit tests that check the UI renders correctly on phones

stem: A team wants to deploy an agent built with an open-source framework to a managed, serverless runtime with session isolation and long-running tasks. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon EC2 instances managed manually
Amazon Lightsail instances per user
AWS Lambda with a 15-minute timeout
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime

stem: An agent must remember user preferences across sessions and summarize past interactions. Which capability fits?

choices.text: A new guardrail that stores user preferences
AgentCore Memory with long-term memory strategies
A higher temperature for more personal responses
A larger context window for every single request

stem: Employees need a secure GenAI assistant over company content in SharePoint and S3, with SSO and permission-aware answers, delivered quickly. Which option fits?

choices.text: A custom chatbot with a shared login and no permission checks
A public model endpoint with all documents pasted into prompts
Amazon Q Business with data source connectors and IAM Identity Center
A search index that ignores document-level access controls

stem: A developer wants the model to call a weather function when needed and receive the result before answering. Which Converse API flow is correct?

choices.text: Provide toolConfig, handle a toolUse stop reason, run the tool, and send toolResult back
Put the weather data in the system prompt for every request in advance
Ask the model to call the weather API itself directly over the internet during generation
Use a knowledge base that stores yesterday's weather for every city

stem: A company exposes a GenAI feature to partners and must limit each partner to 10,000 requests per day. Which feature fits?

choices.text: A Lambda function that counts requests in memory
An S3 bucket policy restricting partner IP addresses
A CloudWatch dashboard showing partner request volumes
API Gateway usage plans with API keys per partner

stem: A children's education app must block sexual content in both prompts and responses at the strictest level. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Guardrail content filters for sexual content set to high on inputs and outputs
A system prompt politely asking the model to avoid inappropriate content
A contextual grounding check with a relevance threshold of 0.9
A word filter containing a few common inappropriate words only

stem: A company wants to confirm that Bedrock does not use its prompts to train foundation models and that data stays in-Region. What is accurate?

choices.text: Bedrock always shares prompts with model providers for their training unless the customer pays an extra fee for an opt-out agreement
Bedrock does not use customer prompts to train base models, and inference stays in the chosen Region unless cross-Region inference is used
Bedrock stores all prompts permanently in a single global location that customers can neither choose nor control in any way
Bedrock sends prompts to every AWS Region automatically to improve availability for each request

stem: A company wants a GenAI feature to reduce support handling time by 30%. Which non-functional requirement is most important to define for the architecture?

choices.text: The date of the next company-wide all-hands meeting
The color of the chat widget in the support console
Target latency and throughput at peak support volumes
The names of the agents who will test the feature first

stem: A financial firm must retain all GenAI interactions for seven years and produce them on legal request within days. Which requirement should drive the logging design?

choices.text: Keeping logs on developers' laptops so they are easy to search
Temporary in-memory storage of recent chat sessions for faster responses
Storing only aggregate token counts per day in a CloudWatch metric
Durable, searchable, tamper-resistant storage of prompts, responses, and metadata

stem: A team must choose between two models that score equally on quality. One costs half as much per token but has twice the latency. The use case is overnight report generation. Which should they choose?

choices.text: The faster model, since latency always outweighs cost in every use case
Neither, since equal quality means the models must be identical anyway
Both, sending each report to both models and paying twice for results
The cheaper model, since latency matters little for overnight batch work

stem: A model must follow a very specific output style that prompting cannot achieve reliably, and 3,000 high-quality examples exist. Which Bedrock option fits?

choices.text: Use a longer system prompt with no examples
Increase temperature to explore more styles
Fine-tune the model with the labeled examples
Continued pre-training on unlabeled web data

stem: A team wants to test a Bedrock model's behavior with different inference parameters before coding. Which approach is quickest?

choices.text: Experiment in the Bedrock console playground
Write a batch inference job for each setting
Deploy a SageMaker endpoint for each setting
Fine-tune a copy of the model for each setting

stem: Source documents have inconsistent date formats in their metadata, breaking date filters in retrieval. Where should this be fixed?

choices.text: In the vector store by disabling all metadata filters for the index
In the ingestion pipeline by normalizing metadata values before indexing
In the user interface by asking users to type dates in several formats
In the generation prompt by asking the model to interpret any date format

stem: A company wants to ingest only documents that pass PII scanning and schema checks, and quarantine the rest for review. Which design fits?

choices.text: A single Lambda function that ingests everything and emails a weekly summary of any problems it found
Direct uploads by users into the knowledge base bucket without any checks
A Step Functions workflow with validation steps that route failures to a quarantine bucket
A nightly job that deletes any documents that failed checks without review

stem: A RAG system needs very low query latency for millions of vectors and in-memory speed. Which option fits?

choices.text: A vector search engine with in-memory indexes, such as Amazon MemoryDB vector search
A nightly batch job that precomputes and stores answers for every possible user query
A relational table with embeddings stored as unindexed text columns
An S3 bucket of CSV files queried by Amazon Athena for every request

stem: A team debates chunk overlap. Which statement about overlap is accurate?

choices.text: Overlap always reduces total storage because the shared text between chunks is stored only once
Overlap preserves context across chunk boundaries at the cost of more storage and tokens
Overlap is required for semantic chunking and forbidden for fixed-size
Overlap has no effect on retrieval quality or on the index size at all

stem: Which TWO signals suggest a RAG system's chunking strategy needs adjustment? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The console displays chunk counts in a small font
The bucket name contains uppercase letters only
The knowledge base was created on a Monday
Retrieved chunks often cut sentences or tables in half
Relevant chunks lack context needed to answer

stem: A knowledge base answer quality varies with how users phrase questions. Which approach improves retrieval robustness?

choices.text: Longer generated answers so that more topics are covered each time
A higher temperature so that answers cover more possible meanings
Fewer documents in the index so that every query matches something
Query reformulation that rewrites questions into clearer search queries

stem: A knowledge base retrieves relevant chunks, but many come from outdated document versions. Which TWO changes help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Switch to a larger generation model with the same retrieved chunks
Remove superseded versions from the data source and re-sync
Increase top-k so newer chunks also appear somewhere in results
Tell users to ignore any answer that seems outdated to them
Filter or boost retrieval by document version or date metadata

stem: A prompt template includes a placeholder for retrieved passages. Which practice keeps prompts effective as retrieval changes?

choices.text: Hard-code sample passages into the template for all requests
Assume the template works for any retrieved content without testing
Test the template against varied retrieval results in the evaluation set
Remove the placeholder and let the model search the web instead

stem: Multiple teams edit shared prompts, causing unreviewed changes in production. Which governance controls help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Restrict who can modify production prompts with IAM permissions
Allow any engineer to edit production prompts directly at any time
Store prompts in chat messages so changes are easy to discuss
Remove versioning to simplify the prompt management process
Require approval workflows before promoting new prompt versions

stem: A prompt asks the model to 'be concise' but responses vary widely in length. Which improvement is most effective?

choices.text: Repeat 'be concise' several times throughout the prompt text
Specify a concrete limit, such as three sentences, and show an example
Remove the instruction so the model decides the best length
Raise the temperature so the model picks a length at random

stem: A company needs to process customer call recordings into searchable, PII-redacted transcripts for a RAG system. Which combination fits?

choices.text: Amazon Rekognition to analyze the audio files and extract topics
Amazon Polly to convert calls into text, then embed the output directly
Amazon Transcribe with PII redaction, then chunk and embed the transcripts
Amazon Translate to convert the audio into English text automatically

stem: Which TWO questions help decide whether a GenAI use case needs RAG, fine-tuning, or only prompting? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Does the answer depend on private or frequently changing information?
What color scheme will the chat interface use for each response?
How many engineers prefer each technique based on personal taste?
Which technique has the most blog posts written about it this year?
Does the task require a style or behavior the base model cannot produce?

stem: A regulated company must run a foundation model entirely within its own VPC boundary with full control over model weights. Which option fits?

choices.text: Use any Bedrock serverless model without any private networking setup
Use a public third-party chatbot website with a corporate account login
Call a model API from another cloud provider over the public internet
Host an open-weight model on SageMaker endpoints inside the company's VPC

stem: A team wants retrieval results to favor recent documents without excluding older ones entirely. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Search only documents created today and ignore everything else
Ask the model to guess which documents are the most recent ones
Delete all documents older than one month from the knowledge base
Boost scores using date metadata while still searching the whole index

stem: A company must isolate vector data for several business units with different access policies while sharing one platform. Which design fits?

choices.text: A single public index accessible to every employee in the company
Separate indexes or collections per unit with access policies on each
Store all vectors in one file and give each unit a copy of it
One shared index with no metadata and trust in application logic

stem: A knowledge base's data source mixes English and Korean documents, and users ask in both languages. Which consideration is most important?

choices.text: Split the index by file size rather than by language support
Use a model that only supports English for faster embedding
Use an embeddings model that supports both languages well
Translate all documents to English and discard the originals

stem: An application must send a large image and text prompt to a multimodal model through a single API regardless of provider. Which approach fits?

choices.text: The Converse API with image and text content blocks
Separate APIs for the image and the text per provider
Uploading the image to a public website for the model
Converting the image into a very long text description

stem: A GenAI feature must degrade gracefully if the model service is unavailable. Which TWO patterns help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A fallback response or alternate model when calls fail
Crashing the application to alert users of the outage
Blocking all user requests until engineers intervene
Infinite retries without delay until the service recovers
A circuit breaker that stops calling a failing endpoint temporarily

stem: A company wants on-premises applications to call a GenAI service in AWS privately. Which connectivity fits?

choices.text: A public S3 bucket where requests are uploaded and polled
Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN into the VPC hosting the service
Email-based requests processed manually by the operations team
Public internet calls with the API key in the URL query string

stem: An agent must access third-party SaaS APIs on behalf of each user with the user's own OAuth consent. Which capability fits?

choices.text: The root user's credentials stored in environment variables
A public API endpoint with no authentication required
A single shared API key embedded in the agent's prompt
AgentCore Identity for managing user-delegated credentials

stem: A knowledge base ingestion job reports failed documents. Where should the engineer look first?

choices.text: The chat UI's front-end code in the browser console
The Route 53 records for the company's public domain
The ingestion job's failure details and logs for each document
